transcript:
Header: 2026-02-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Attendees: Elena (Redwood), Samir (Redwood SE), Karen (Redwood Partnerships), Alicia (Polaris), Tom (Polaris), Priya (Polaris SE), Noah (Polaris Ops)

Summary: Quick weekly sync to review co-sell pipeline and align on next actions. A few deals flagged for immediate benchmarking and legal introductions.

[00:00] Elena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - we got Polaris leadership and ops - can you hear me ok?
[00:06] Alicia (Polaris): Yep all good, thanks Elena.
[00:08] Tom (Polaris): Good to be here.
[00:10] Samir (Redwood SE): Hey team, Samir here, I'll jump into the technical asks after the pipeline review.
[00:15] Priya (Polaris SE): Priya on my side. We have a few deals where customers asked about private deployments and SOC two evidences.

[00:28] Elena (Redwood AE): Great. Agenda: 1) run through your top ten co-sell targets 2) call out which ones need an SE deep-dive or benchmarks 3) legal/comp questions 4) next steps. We'll keep this tight.
[00:40] Noah (Polaris Ops): Sounds good. We'll start with Deal A - large fintech. Tom is owner.

[01:02] Tom (Polaris): Deal A is a mid-market fintech, in RFP stage. They care about latency and data residency. They asked whether we can do VPC/private deployment or if only hosted API is available. Also they want SOC 2 and logs.
[01:18] Elena (Redwood AE): Good to call that out. For Redwood we offer hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For regulated fin serv customers Private is usually the ask. Note - our private offering supports customer-managed networking and KMS integration.
[01:36] Priya (Polaris SE): small transcription glitch there in my notes - you said KMS integration; customer specifically asked about HSM support. Is that on roadmap?
[01:45] Samir (Redwood SE): We do KMS today; HSM is available via partner KMS integrations for higher tiers, we can map that in the doc. I'll include the exact security matrix in the deck.

[02:10] Alicia (Polaris): Deal B is a health-tech prospect with data residency concerns - they asked about on-prem/offline modes.
[02:18] Elena: For health care customers we've done private deployments, can do air-gapped on-prem packaging in some cases. That requires legal + infra lead times typically 8 to 12 weeks.

[02:38] Tom: Timeline question - our customer wants to pilot in 4-6 weeks. Can Redwood hit that with a pilot on hosted but with strict retention?
[02:48] Samir: Yes, pilot on hosted is fastest; we can enforce shorter retention windows, custom RBAC, and audit logs. For a full Private deployment the 8-12 week estimate stands. Pilot on hosted with a dedicated pool could meet the 4-6 week ask.

[03:12] Elena: We'll call that out as an option - hosted pilot then migrate to private if they win the deal.

[03:28] Priya: Deal C - retailer - cares about token costs and throughput at peak sale days. They asked about quantization and batching recommendations.
[03:36] Samir: Right. For high throughput e-comm we recommend model quantization (4-bit/8-bit depending on model), continuous batching, and prefix KV caching. That typically reduces per-token cost 3x to 5x on typical workloads. We'll share quantization profiles we've validated.
[03:58] Priya: Can you include perf numbers for the Mistral-ish models? Customer asked specifically about costs vs Anthropic.
[04:06] Samir: We'll include a benchmark that compares lat/throughput and cost estimates across a few open models. Note - some of the model names in the deck might be auto-transcribed; we'll make sure the customer-facing docs use proper model IDs.

[04:30] Noah: A question on routing - Polaris asks if we can route traffic by latency or cost policy. That matters for multi-region customers.
[04:38] Elena: Yes, Redwood supports smart routing policies, region and tier-based. We can do policy-based routing with automatic fallback to compatible variants. Good to show that as a diagram in the enablement deck.

[04:50] Alicia: On comp: Polaris wants clarity on co-sell motion and commission splits for referrals vs joint-sell. Can we codify that?
[05:00] Karen (Redwood Partnerships): We have standard co-sell guidelines; I'll share the partner playbook with comp examples. For larger enterprise motions we typically have negotiated splits, and we'll introduce legal to discuss carve-outs.

[05:18] Tom: For Deal D there's a perf ask - they want a hard SLA on p95 latency under 400ms at 256 tokens.
[05:26] Samir: We can size Dedicated capacity to get that p95, but we need exact concurrency and sequence length distribution. I'll put together a sizing sheet. If customer is sensitive to cost we can show a cost-vs-latency tradeoff.

[05:46] Elena: Mark Deal D as candidate for Dedicated + canary rollout. Which of you will own the pilot intro?
[05:52] Tom: I'll own the customer intro - I'll send contact details after the call.

[06:06] Priya: A few prospects asked about our security certifications - do we have up-to-date SOC 2 and ISO? Also they asked about audit logs and data retention policy.
[06:18] Elena: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and pursuing ISO 27001; we have detailed audit logs per request and retention policies that we can configure. I'll attach the security pack in the follow up.
[06:30] Priya: Can you include sample audit log output? Our security team likes to see schemas.
[06:36] Samir: Yes I'll attach sample log schema and the KMS integration diagram. Expect that in the deck.

[06:50] Alicia: A quick legal note - certain buyers want explicit indemnities and data residency clauses. Polaris legal will need to review your draft MSA.
[06:58] Karen: Understood. We'll provide a redline-friendly MSA and annotate sections that typically need negotiation.

[07:12] Tom: On GTM - what's the suggested customer-facing pitch? Are we joint-run demos or Polaris-led with Redwood as a co-seller?
[07:22] Elena: We recommend a joint-run demo for the first call and then handoff to Polaris sales for closing. Redwood AE attends key meetings for technical and contractual support. We'll co-brand decks and provide a one-page playbook for Polaris reps.

[07:40] Priya: For Deal E there's a question about on-prem inference hardware - customer asked what GPUs we support and if Redwood supports model compilation for older Ampere-based infra.
[07:52] Samir: We support a broad matrix - Ampere, Hopper, and some Tegra types. Our compilation layer picks kernels based on arch and sequence length. For older hardware we can produce optimized kernels but need extra validation time. We'll include a compatibility matrix.

[08:22] Noah: A practical ask - Polaris wants a single spreadsheet with all co-sell deals, stages, owners, ask bits (security, pilot, legal), and recommended Redwood asset. Can we get that by Friday?
[08:34] Elena: Yes - we'll produce a co-sell pipeline spreadsheet and populate the top 10 deals you shared. We'll send by 2026-02-20.

[09:00] Tom: One of the buyers mentioned concern about vendor lock-in and ability to switch models or run on their own infra later. How do you address that?
[09:10] Samir: Our platform supports model variants and encourages open-model usage - customers can pull weights and run on-prem if contract allows; we also provide model catalog and export options. We'll highlight portability guarantees in the materials.

[09:34] Alicia: Competitor question - some prospects compare to Anthropic and OpenAI; they ask about cost and safety guardrails. How do you position?
[09:44] Elena: Position: we emphasize production economics and deployment flexibility. For safety, we provide rate limits, content filters, and custom moderation hooks. We'll let the SEs show perf and safety tradeoffs in the benchmark appendix.

[10:01] Priya: Quick note - please avoid auto-transcribed product names in the slide deck; our security team gets confused when it's "Redwood Privat" in notes.
[10:10] Karen: Noted, we'll QA the deck before sending.

[10:22] Tom: For Deal B health-tech, can we have a joint discovery with the buyer's security team? They want to meet security engineers.
[10:30] Elena: Yes - Samir and I can join a 60-minute security deep dive. Propose next Tuesday 2026-02-25 - does that work?
[10:40] Priya: That works for us, I'll confirm internally.

[10:50] Samir: For the benchmark scope - I want to propose two scenarios: 1) latency-focused (p95 under 400ms, 256 tokens) and 2) throughput-focused (sustained 200 qps at burst). We'll run tests on our Dedicated and a hosted config to compare.
[11:06] Tom: Good. Make sure you include cost per 1M tokens estimates for each config.
[11:12] Samir: Will do. Also note that some model names customers referenced may be misspelled in their RFPs; we'll confirm model IDs.

[11:28] Alicia: Anything else on pipeline?
[11:32] Tom: Deal F - small startup - just needs demo + sandbox access; they asked for developer docs and early account.
[11:38] Elena: We can grant sandbox access via a dev account and attach a usage quota for safety. I'll include quickstart links in the follow up.

[11:50] Priya: For sales enablement - Polaris asked about a one-pager on recommended qualification questions. Can you provide that?
[11:58] Karen: Yes, we'll provide a reps one-pager and 2 slide demo template.

[12:10] Noah: On championing - we want to identify an internal Polaris champion for each deal. We'll include that column in the pipeline spreadsheet.

[12:20] Elena: Good idea. We'll add 'Polaris owner' and 'Redwood owner' columns.
[12:30] Tom: Any blockers on your side?
[12:34] Samir: Main blocker is details for benchmarking - concurrency and payloads. Once Polaris shares real request patterns we can size Dedicated correctly.

[12:48] Priya: We'll anonymize and share payload histograms.

[13:00] Elena: Recap of next steps: Elena/Karen send enablement deck + playbook + pipeline spreadsheet by 2026-02-20; Samir to produce benchmark plan and run tests for Deal B + D with results by 2026-03-03; Polaris to share top 10 deals and contact owners by 2026-02-23; legal intros and MSA redlines to be coordinated by 2026-02-25.

[13:28] Alicia: Sounds good. Thanks team.
[13:32] Tom: I'll send the Deal D contact and pipeline list after the call.
[13:36] Elena: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up in email and I'll post the deck in the partner channel.
[13:42] Priya: Thanks all.

[13:45] End of call.

Notes: transcript contains small transcription errors (e.g., "SOC two" vs "SOC 2", "Redwood Privat") typical of automated captures. Attachments referenced: co-sell enablement deck (link TBD), security pack (SOC2 report summary), pipeline spreadsheet (template).
questions: Can Redwood support HSM integrations for KMS?
What is the typical timeline for private/on-prem deployments?
Can Redwood provide p95 latency benchmarks for p95 <400ms at 256 tokens?
What security artifacts (SOC2/ISO) are available for partners to share?
